source.text: The hottest fuel of the stack, the hottest slice's. Slice 4 of 9 (centre at 0.1905 m, heat rate 31.416 kW/m, coolant 573 K): the closed-form series solution of that slice gives 1727.9346 K at the centre. The power shape is a cosine, normalised to an average of 1 (the slice at the middle has (pi/2) cos(0) = 1.571 of the average). The solver's slices exchange a little heat along the height, which this solution does not have, so the tolerance is the sum of: the mesh bound 5 x 833.33 K / 100^2 = 0.417 K; the axial conduction allowance 3 x 0.00099 (the estimate as a fraction of the largest rise) x 1154.9 K (the largest rise of any slice above its coolant) = 3.415 K; the cosine's 41-point table, 1e-3 of the slice's rise of 1154.9 K = 1.155 K; rounded up to 0.05 K (5 K), fixed before any run.
source.check: Second method: FEED's own per-slice closed form (src/core/closedForm.ts through axialSummary, tests/seedOracleStack.test.ts, to 1e-3 K apart from the cosine's table term), and the real solver (FEED_SOLVER=1): every check of the run passes and the solver's slice peaks are inside the tolerances.

coverage.domain: synthetic pin (constant conductivities, convective boundary 573 K and 30000 W/m2/K on every slice) as 9 radial slices over 0.381 m with a cosine power shape, 20 kW/m on average (31.4 kW/m at the peak)
